messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert generated for dedicated-us-east-2 - autoscaler unable to provision beyond reserved capacity, request queue growth observed, aggregate QPS ~72k, p95 latency >800ms for text.generate. Paging oncall.

sarah (oncall): on it. do we have a live customer hit list? @lee can you confirm which Dedicated customers are showing errors/latency?

lee (customer-ops): three customers report elevated errors (500s) and timeouts: acct-824, acct-phi, acct-rapid. All on dedicated-us-east-2 pools. I've flagged CS to open tickets, telling customers we're investigating. No public status page update yet.

mike (sre): adding quick notes: autoscaler logs show failures to allocate new nodes due to quota check failing when capacity > reserved commit. control-plane is returning 409 on scale requests. suspect policy guardrail kicking in. Also seeing many long-lived streaming connections holding slots.

jordan (eng-platform): confirmed - rollout earlier today tightened max-burst to reserved+0. We pushed new RBAC guard accidentally. Reverting now.

sarah (oncall): mitigation plan (short):
- enable burst capacity toggle for dedicated-us-east-2 to allow emergency overtime scaling
- immediately apply temporary per-customer concurrency cap  (reduce from 250 -> 50)
- add global soft rate-limit for non-SLA customers at 60r/s
- disable large-context model variants that increase kernel memory (degrade quality but reduce resource use)
- prepare rollback of RBAC guard if toggle fails

mike (sre): commands I'm about to run, posting for audit:

```
# enable burst capacity (emergency)
rwctl dedicated pools update --pool dedicated-us-east-2 --burst enabled --reason "SEV2 emergency"

# patch per-customer concurrency override
rwctl tenants update-concurrency --tenant acct-* --max-concurrency 50 --region us-east-2

# soft global rate limit for non-sla
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://control.redwood/api/v1/traffic/rules -d '{"scope":"non-sla","limit_rps":60,"duration_s":60}'
```

sarah (oncall): :thumbsup: mike execute. jordan coordinate rollback path with platform. lee, please prepare customer outbound templates with ETA ~20-40m and the mitigation steps we're taking.

ops-bot: rwctl task 5421 created by mike: enabling burst for dedicated-us-east-2. ETA for node provisioning ~ 120s per instance.

mike (sre): burst toggle applied, control-plane returned ACCEPTED. provisioning starting, watch logs: `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=autoscaler --since=5m`.

jordan (eng-platform): I'm reverting the RBAC guard that prevents scale beyond commit. Patch diff below:

```
- if (requested > reservedCommit) reject();
+ if (requested > reservedCommit && !emergencyBurstEnabled) reject();
```

jordan (eng-platform): patch applied and rolled out to control-plane 2 minutes ago. autoscaler requests now accepted.

sarah (oncall): seeing p95 latency drop from 820ms -> 420ms over the last 3 minutes. queue length decreasing. how many extra nodes came up?

mike (sre): +6 nodes, ~15% extra capacity. Still throttling some streaming sessions. I'll continue draining very long-lived streams into batched worker mode.

lee (customer-ops): customer comms updated and sent to affected accounts: short note, what we changed, expected improvements, invite to contact CS if they see continued errors. No major escalations yet.

sarah (oncall): mid-mitigation checklist:
- [x] burst enabled
- [x] RBAC guard reverted
- [x] per-tenant concurrency cap applied
- [x] soft rate-limit rule in place
- [x] customer comms sent
- [ ] monitor for next 30m, prepare rollback of surge changes after stabilization

mike (sre): follow-up action: create a hotfix to autoscaler policy to permit emergency bursts when flagged by ops, and add better error telemetry (409 -> more context). Tracking issue: PLAT-3321

jordan (eng-platform): adding an automated fallback: if provisioning fails for 60s, route new Dedicated requests to compatible hosted model pool (best-effort) with reduced throughput. Implementing now as a short-circuit.

sarah (oncall): handoff plan: I'm oncall for another 28m then handing to mike. I'll summarize in the oncall handoff channel and update runbook with the burst toggle steps.

mike (sre): standing by for handoff. If anything regresses, escalate to oncall pager, and we will temporarily disable large-context variants of `redwood-large` across dedicated pools (breaking change for a few customers but better than sustained errors).

incident-bot: SEV2 -> now classified as mitigated (partial) at 1764503120. Continue monitoring for reoccurrence.

sarah (oncall): marking thread as 'mitigated - monitoring'. leaving a note for next oncall: check rwctl task 5421 completion, PLAT-3321 status, and verify no remaining 409s in control-plane logs. cc @mike (sre) who will pick up.

mike (sre): taking handoff. I'll keep watches for 60m and then update the incident log. Thanks all.

ops-bot: Incident runbook entry created: incidents/1764501123 - autoscaler burst toggle & temporary traffic shaping. Tags: dedicated, autoscaling, mitigation, followup:PLAT-3321

sarah (oncall): :wave: handing off. good job team.

lee (customer-ops): closing customer tickets with follow-up note once we confirm no further errors. will reopen if customers report anything else.

mike (sre): final note before I close monitoring: consider adding automated throttles based on queue length not just CPU/GPU signals; queue-based autoscaling rule could have prevented this. filing follow-up task.

sarah (oncall): agreed. adding to runbook improvements. "queue-length -> preemptive burst" rule.
